prompt: packages/japanese/prompts/reading-validator.md, applied per item: read the passage alone, answer the stem from the passage, then mark each option CORRECT / WRONG / UNCERTAIN; exactly one option in CORRECT or UNCERTAIN is PASS, two or more is AMBIGUOUS, none is UNANSWERABLE.
note: Round A, judge family 1 over the 8-row authored N3 長文 batch (key-less packet .cache/judge/choubun-n3-blind.md, verdicts in .cache/judge/choubun-n3-familyA.md, frozen keys .cache/judge/choubun-n3-keys.json). All 8 rows PASS and all 8 picks equal the frozen key (8/8), verified by parsing the verdict blocks rather than by reading the judge's summary. Unlike the N1 長文 batch these keys are NOT words the passage prints: each is a paraphrase of a deciding sentence the row also cites in its own `evidence` field, which is what makes a blind re-answer a real test of the item rather than a test of the mask.

prompt: same 8 items, deliberately different procedure: judged in REVERSE packet order (item 8 first), and for every item all four options were argued from the passage text as steelmans before any verdict was assigned, reporting every option that survives its own steelman.
note: Round B, judge family 2 over the same batch (verdicts in .cache/judge/choubun-n3-familyB.md): all 8 rows PASS, surviving option equal to the frozen key on every row (16/16 across both families). The adversarial pass named the near-misses and dismissed each on passage text: n3b-8's 準備を手伝う staffing reading is broken by two different printed motives plus 三人目は何も言わず, n3b-7's notebook reading by sequence (その週のあと places it after the utterance 『それ』 answers), n3b-5's 会場 option by a merge of two separate deadlines (the venue receives the PHOTOS, the reply goes to the writer), n3b-3's 三十六度 figure by belonging to the pre-planting grass measurement rather than the stated night-cooling mechanism. No row is burned. THE LIMIT OF BOTH RECORDS, stated so this file is not read as stronger than it is: these two passes are the same model family as the author of the rows, so their agreement is correlated error rather than independent confirmation, and nothing here catches a key that is wrong in a way the authoring model also believes. There is no further leg to add: nobody in this project reads Japanese, so no human can check whether a passage decides its key, and a translated review sheet would only ask a reader to agree with the model's own translation. Such a sheet existed here and was deleted as a formality, not as evidence. The mechanical screens in check-reading-choubun.ts decide shape and self-citation only; the coverage floor is deliberately not among them (doc-27 §10), because the official N3 長文 itself scores 88.9% under it.
